answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Continuity Scoring. Each identity must reproduce its prior epoch's interaction signature within a tolerance band, checked at each zenith of the scoring cycle. Sudden shifts—new peer sets, altered timing, fresh task mixes—trigger decay unless consistent across a gale of successive epochs. Payouts vest only after three matching epochs, so a sybil farmer must sustain many parallel identities through repeated costly verification rounds, multiplying compute and time per successful clone. Any vine of linked identities that breaks continuity forfeits accrued rewards.
